name: What is the difference between tenant improvement and commercial remodel?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between a tenant improvement and a commercial remodel?
mainEntity.text: What is the difference between a tenant improvement and a commercial remodel?

acceptedAnswer.text: Tenant improvement work is typically focused on customizing an existing leased space for a specific business use. That can include new partitions, lighting, finishes, restrooms, HVAC adjustments, and code-required upgrades. A commercial remodel is a broader term that may describe improvements to an occupied building, whether for a tenant, owner-user, or property repositioning effort. In practice, the distinction matters because permit scope, design coordination, and budget can change significantly based on whether the work is cosmetic, code-driven, or structural. In markets like Los Angeles, Glendale, Pasadena, Burbank, and North Hollywood, owners should clarify who is responsible for base building conditions, what the lease requires, and whether the project affects life safety, accessibility, or egress. That distinction also helps determine whether the work is best handled as a fast interior alteration or a more complex phased remodel with multiple trades and inspections.
acceptedAnswer.description: A tenant improvement usually refers to work inside an existing commercial space to fit a new occupant’s needs, such as offices, retail, or restaurants. A commercial remodel is broader and may include reconfiguring layouts, upgrading finishes, systems, or sometimes exterior elements. Tenant improvements are often tied to lease requirements and occupancy needs.
